{{Use British English|date=November 2018}}

'''Friedrich Bachmann''' (11 February 1909 – 1 October 1982<ref name="math">{{cite web |last1=O'Connor |first1=J J |last2=Robertson |first2=E F |title=Friedrich Bachmann |url=http://www-history.mcs.st-and.ac.uk/Biographies/Bachmann_Friedrich.html |website=School of Mathematics and Statistics |publisher=University of St Andrews |accessdate=18 November 2018 |date=July 2009}}</ref>) was a German mathematician who specialised in [[geometry]] and [[group theory]].<ref name="gen">{{mathgenealogy|id=18609}}</ref>

==Life==
Bachmann was the son of a [[Lutheranism|Lutheran]] minister Hans Bachmann. Bachmann came from an intellectual family, his paternal grandfather was the [[Number theory|number theorist]] [[Paul Gustav Heinrich Bachmann]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=O'Connor |first1=J J |last2=Robertson |first2=E F |title=Friedrich Bachmann |url=https://mathshistory.st-andrews.ac.uk/Biographies/Bachmann_Friedrich/ |website=MacTutor |publisher=School of Mathematics and Statistics, University of St Andrews, Scotland |access-date=27 January 2022 |date=July 2009}}</ref> Bachmann took his early education at the [[Gymnasium (Germany)|Gymnasium]] in [[Münster]]. After attending the Gymnasium, he attended the [[University of Münster]] and the [[Humboldt University of Berlin]] and graduated in 1927. While there he was a member of the [[Wingolf|Münster Wingolfs]].<ref name="math"/>

In 1933, Bachmann was promoted to [[Doctor of Philosophy|D.Phil]] with a thesis titled, ''Studies on the foundation of arithmetic with special reference to [[Richard Dedekind|Dedekind]], [[Gottlob Frege|Frege]], and [[Bertrand Russell|Russell]]'' ({{langx|de|Untersuchungen zur Grundlegung der Arithmetik mit besonderer Beziehung auf Dedekind, Frege, und Russell}}). His advisor was [[Heinrich Scholz]].<ref name="math"/>

His doctoral students include [[Andreas Dress]] and [[Rolf Lingenberg]].<ref name="math"/>

Bachmann  was married to a great-granddaughter of [[Otto von Bismarck]], Alexandra von Bredow. They had a son together, Sebastian<ref name="math"/>

==Career==
In 1935, Bachmann moved to the [[University of Marburg]] where assisted [[Kurt Reidemeister]]. Bachman [[habilitation|habilitated]] at Marburg before becoming a  [[Privatdozent]] in 1939.<ref name="math"/>

From 1941 Bachmann became a private lecturer at [[University of Königsberg]] and from 1943 at the [[Humboldt University of Berlin]].

On 1 March 1949, he was promoted to full professor ([[Ordentlicher Professor]]) at the [[University of Kiel]]. He became known for his work on geometry, especially for his axiomatic justification of elementary geometry with mirroring operations, previously begun by [[Johannes Hjelmslev]] and others.<ref name="math"/>

After the war, Bachmann worked with the mathematician [[Karl-Heinrich Weise]] to rebuild the mathematics department at the [[University of Kiel]].
From 1960 Bachman was editor of the series titled, ''Grundzüge der Mathematik für Lehrer an Gymnasien sowie für Mathematiker in Industrie und Wirtschaft'' (Basic features of mathematics for teachers at grammar schools as well as for mathematicians in industry and business).<ref name="math"/>

In 1962–1963, Bachmann was elected [[Dean (education)|Dean]] of the mathematics department of the Faculty of Philosophy of Kiel University.<ref name="math"/>

Bachmann retired on 31 March 1977.
